newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures hold late gains on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures hold late gains on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures held modest gains late Tuesday in sluggish activity, with forecasts for mostly below-normal East Coast and Midwest temperatures into next week still underpinning the complex.
At 1415 EST, January climbed 5.6 cents to $3.55 per million British thermal units, while February was 3.9 cents higher at $3.085. Other months were up by 2.9 to seven cents.

"The market remembers last year vividly and storage is still on the low side. Until we see a change in the weather, you've got to like the market," said one Houston trader, referring to last winter's price spikes on record low storage.

Traders said revised 6-10-day forecasts calling for more below-normal Midwest and Northeast weather next week were likely to support the early December cash and keep the bears on the sidelines near-term.
But some expected a dip before the long, holiday weekend.
"I think cash and futures could come off some before the (U.S. Thanksgiving Day) holiday because we don't have the industrial demand," said another Houston-based trader.
NYMEX will be closed Thursday and Friday for the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday.
Technically, traders still pegged support in January in the mid-$3.20s and then at $3.04. Resistance remained at the $3.68 contract high.

Cash sources said November Gulf Coast gas firmed Tuesday by 15-20 cents to the high-$3.80s, with December on the same pipes notionally little changed in the low-to-mid $3.80s. November Midwest prices were steady to down slightly at about $3.80, with December notionally unchanged to lower at $3.80. December gas at the New York city gate was thinly talked around $5.00.
NYMEX said 16,971 Hub contracts traded at 1350 EST. Hub open interest on Nov 25 fell 2,085 contracts to 140,566.
NYMEX Alberta natgas was still untraded at 1415 EST. Alberta open interest on Nov 25 fell 39 lots to 448.
NYMEX Permian natgas also was untraded at 1415 EST. Permian open interest on Nov 25 fell 15 contracts to 502.
NYMEX December Alberta and Permian natgas expire today.

On the KCBT, January was up six cents at $3.33 after hitting a new high of $3.34. Feb was seven cents higher at $2.90, also a new high. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.4 cent to 22 cents (NYMEX premium).
